notes.note: WebGL content on macOS is now rendered using Apple's Metal graphics API, which can improve performance on some sites.

In [Smart Window][1], Organize Tabs is now available in French. Firefox can suggest groups of related open tabs and name each group in the language of your tabs.


  [1]: https://www.firefox.com/smart-window

Added a new playback speed setting to the [Picture-in-Picture][1] player, with options ranging from 0.25x to 2.0x speed. Please note that the setting is only visible on medium or larger player windows.


  [1]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/about-picture-picture-firefox
You can now drag history entries from the sidebar to the tab strip to open them in new tabs.
The address bar context menu now shows "Paste and Search" instead of "Paste and Go" when the copied text is a search term rather than a web address.
PDFs created when saving a page as PDF now include MathML content that is accessible to assistive technology such as screen readers.
Websites that repeatedly ask to open email (mailto:) and other links in a web apps can now be blocked with a new “Never allow” button, and blocked sites can be managed in Settings.

Mini Window lets you move a tab or a selected part of a page into an always-on-top window while you browse. We’d appreciate your feedback on [Mozilla Connect][1] as we develop and improve this early version of the feature.

  [1]: https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/discussions/mini-window-is-going-live-in-firefox-160-and-we-want-your/m-p/144137#M59048

On [Firefox for Android][1], Local Network Access restrictions are now enabled by default. Firefox now requires websites to request your permission before connecting to devices on your local network or to apps and services on your device.

  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.firefox_beta
Firefox now plays Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio.
Increased the contrast between the domain name and the rest of the address in the address bar, making it easier to understand which website you're viewing.

The recognition side of the [Web Speech API][1] is now implemented, performing on-device real-time Speech-to-text in 40 languages


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Web_Speech_API
Firefox now supports the legacy `::-webkit-input-placeholder` pseudo-element as an alias of `::placeholder`, to improve compatibility with websites that use it to style placeholder text.
Fixed the first character typed into the address bar or search bar sometimes being lost when typing quickly right after clicking into it.
Fixed Firefox freezing for several seconds when signing in to intranet sites that use NTLM or Kerberos (Negotiate) authentication.
Fixed downloaded files on macOS sometimes opening in the wrong application instead of the default one set in Finder.
Fixed links opened in the background from other apps on macOS, such as RSS readers, bringing Firefox to the foreground.
Fixed situations where only the first of several simultaneous downloads showed a save dialog on macOS when Firefox is set to ask where to save files, and only downloaded the first file.

On [Firefox for Android][1], web addresses containing non-Latin characters are now shown in readable form in the address bar and elsewhere in the app, instead of as encoded text.

  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.firefox_beta

On [Firefox for Android][1], fixed web addresses containing spaces, such as those from scanned QR codes, being searched for instead of opened.

  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.firefox_beta

On [Firefox for Android][1], fixed the touch actions near the cursor position in a text field, including double-tapping and long-tapping to select a word, and single-tapping to place the cursor.

  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.firefox_beta
Restored meaningful filenames and the usual save workflow for PDFs opened in Preview from the macOS print dialog.

system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Beta gets updated 3 times a week and as a consequence, the release notes for the Beta channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports.
Warning: Features listed here may or may not make a final release of Firefox

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development via the [Firefox Trains][1] website or our [@FirefoxBeta][2] Bluesky account. [1]: https://whattrainisitnow.com/beta/ [2]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxbeta.bsky.social
